title: When the Border Turns
premise: Mirabel Vane, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a false name in a coastal town, receives calls on a burner phone she never bought from her sister Delia—who died eight years ago. The voice leads her to a buried dossier proving the three agencies that fired her all laundered the same black-site money, and that Delia faked her death to protect it. Hunted by an assassin named Corvus and betrayed by her last remaining ally, Mirabel must smuggle the dossier onto a dawn extraction flight while deciding whether the 'sister' on the phone is truly Delia or a trap stitched from her own grief. In the end, Mirabel trades the dossier's public release for Delia's surrender to the authorities, boards the flight with neither file nor sister but with a found family of fellow castoffs—and finally unpacks the go-bag.
about_author: Sebastian Ashgrove is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent a decade moving people and cargo across borders he was never cleared to ask about. He writes thrillers about the people who fall through institutional cracks and build their own nets.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Establishes her exile in Grayhaven Cove: three agencies, three firings, a fake name, a packed bag by the door. She breaks her own rule by helping a neighbor's kid, showing the belonging she pretends not to want. The burner phone rings; the voice is Delia's. Emotional beat: dread laced with unbearable hope.

chapters.title: Eight Years of Static
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, flashback-woven. She verifies the voice against old family recordings and confirms it's real—or a perfect forgery. Delia gives her a dead-drop location and one warning: trust no one who knew her before Grayhaven. Mirabel retrieves a partial dossier page. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvus Arrives
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the assassin Corvus, elegant and patient, traces the dead-drop traffic to the coast. Mirabel notices surveillance tradecraft she herself once ran. She preps escape routes but can't leave—the next call promises proof of how Delia 'died.' Beat: hunter and hunted circling the same wound.

chapters.title: The Castoff Network
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Forced to run, she taps a hidden network of exiled analysts, smugglers, and forgers—people like her, discarded by the same machine. They shelter her in a safehouse above a fish cannery. First real taste of found family. Beat: cautious warmth she doesn't know how to accept.

chapters.title: What Delia Buried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV with Delia interludes. The full dossier surfaces: all three agencies funneled black-site funds through the same shell, and Delia discovered it, faked her death, and spent eight years assembling evidence. But one page is missing—the one naming who ordered Delia silenced. Beat: vindication curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Ally Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her old mentor, Sable, resurfaces offering extraction help. Mirabel, starving for trust, nearly hands over the dossier—until the castoffs catch Sable feeding coordinates to Corvus. Confrontation in the cannery; Sable escapes with a decoy drive. Beat: betrayal confirming her oldest scar.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Multi-POV chapter: agency handlers in three capitals quietly agree to bury the dossier and let Corvus finish the job, each protecting their share. Meanwhile Mirabel decodes the missing page's location—it's been on the burner phone itself all along. Beat: the walls closing in, the truth closer than expected.

chapters.title: Corvus at the Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Corvus breaches the safehouse at night. Instead of fighting, Mirabel talks—recognizing another discarded asset, offering him a place in the story instead of a grave. He hesitates, wounds her, and lets her go, compromised himself now. Beat: mercy as a tactical act and a personal turning point.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. At the airfield, Delia appears in person—but so do Sable and agency retrieval teams. Mirabel broadcasts the dossier to every news desk mid-standoff, making it worthless to suppress. Delia chooses surrender over flight; Corvus covers their retreat from Sable. Beat: sacrifice, exposure, and the truth finally past all three governments.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, months later. Delia awaits trial; the agencies are under investigation; the castoff network becomes Mirabel's real employer. She visits Delia through glass, then returns home and, in the final image, empties the go-bag into a dresser drawer. Beat: belonging chosen at last—inherited not by blood, but by staying.
